title: Doubled pawns: count what they buy
outcomes: Finds doubled pawns by the app's definition (two or more pawns of one colour on a file)
Lists what can compensate for them: the bishop pair, an open or half-open file, central control
Sees how one changed piece (bishop to knight) changes that list
Checks whether an opponent's recapture leaves the pawns doubled, in three unlabeled positions; whether to accept lasting doubled pawns is not tested here

steps.text: In this app, pawns are **doubled** when two or more pawns of one colour stand on the same file. They are weak mainly when they advance or are stuck and isolated; while they stay still they can be useful. Rule of thumb: look for what they buy (the bishop pair, a half-open file, central control) before counting a loss. See also 'Weak pawns: targets only if you can attack them'.

**Rule of thumb, with conditions.** Doubled pawns tend to be acceptable with the bishop pair, a half-open file or central control, and while they stay still. They are a problem when isolated, blocked or forced to advance. 'Always bad' is false, and so is 'never matters'. The next positions change one feature at a time.

steps.title: Doubled pawns and the bishop pair
steps.prompt: Predict which statement fits, then check. In the second position one Black bishop became a knight; in the third a Black pawn is gone, so nobody has doubled pawns.
When a capture would double your pawns, what do you now check first: does the opponent just recapture, or do the doubled pawns stay? Write your own short list.
